events.title: Richard Hamming publishes error-correcting codes
events.summary: Richard Hamming published error-detecting and error-correcting codes in 1950 — including the Hamming code used in memory and storage.
events.about: Hamming codes let systems detect and fix single-bit errors — foundational for reliable RAM, CDs, and telecommunications. The story goes Hamming invented them out of frustration when a computer dropped his weekend runs.

narrative.whyChosen: Hamming codes are the entry point to error correction in computing curricula.
narrative.whyImportant: They made unreliable hardware usable for critical computation.
narrative.problemSolved: Early computers could not trust stored bits without detection and recovery.
